Across four independent pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (KEGG + WikiPathways + Reactome), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and the Reactome Reactome hierarchical ORA — tryptophan metabolism ranks as the top hit with FDR scores between 10⁻⁸ and 10⁻¹⁵. Across four independent pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (KEGG + WikiPathways + Reactome), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and the Reactome Reactome hierarchical ORA — tryptophan metabolism ranks as the top hit with FDR scores between 10⁻⁸ and 10⁻¹⁵. The KEGG pathway hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) is the consensus leader (RaMP rank 1, FDR 3.4 × 10⁻¹⁵; MetaboAnalystR rank 1, p = 5.4 × 10⁻⁹), with a fold-enrichment of 750.6 and six input metabolites mapping onto 41 pathway members. The WikiPathways analogue WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism, RaMP rank 2, FDR 4.1 × 10⁻¹⁵) confirms the same signal. Within this axis, three sub-pathways show distinct biological signatures: the serotonin–melatonin branch (Reactome R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.6 × 10⁻⁸) captures L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin; the biogenic-amine synthesis module (WikiPathways WP:WP550, FDR 4.0 × 10⁻⁸) implicates the same three intermediates; and the tryptophan→NAD⁺ catabolic shunt (WikiPathways WP:WP4210, FDR 6.9 × 10⁻⁸) is anchored by 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (C00078, CHEBI:16828), its direct decarboxylation product tryptamine (C00398, CHEBI:16765), the transamination product indoleacetaldehyde (C00637, CHEBI:18086), and the three downstream effectors serotonin (C00780, CHEBI:28790), melatonin (C01598, CHEBI:16796), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632, CHEBI:15793). The remaining inputs — molybdenum atom (C00150), 4-hydroxyglutamate (C05947), 3-aminopropanal (C05665), and all-trans-4-hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) — are either singletons in their respective pathways (retinoic acid p = 0.08, 3-aminopropanal p = 0.10) or not enriched, consistent with treatment specificity focused on the indole-tryptophan axis. Biologically, these results indicate that the treatment diverts tryptophan flux away from or toward the kynurenine–NAD⁺ branch (signalled by 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid accumulation) and the serotonin–melatonin neuroendocrine axis, with potential implications for immune regulation, circadian signalling, and oxidative-stress response.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the primary affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" at rank 1 (FDR = 3.4e-15, 6 metabolite hits including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and indoleacetaldehyde) and the corresponding WikiPathways analogue WP:WP465 at rank 2 (FDR = 4.1e-15, same 6-hit set). Mummichog's m/z-direct analysis returned "Tryptophan metabolism" (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) as its top hit (p = 0.0017, 13 of 14 pathway compounds matched), and MetaboAnalystR PSEA returned hsa00380 (KEGG Tryptophan metabolism) as rank 1 (p = 5.4e-09, 6 hits). This constitutes a clean triple-paradigm consensus. A secondary, weaker signal from Vitamin A metabolism emerged via 4-hydroxyretinoic acid: mummichog ranked "Vitamin A (retinol) metabolism" at position 5 (p = 0.048), and MetaboAnalystR listed KEGG hsa00830 (Retinol metabolism) at rank 2 (p = 0.0825). InChIKey reconciliation confirmed that all eight structurally resolved input metabolites are distinct compounds with no cross-namespace structural conflicts. The tryptophan-axis driver metabolites span the full breadth of the pathway: the substrate L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), the decarboxylation product tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), the transamination intermediate indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637), the downstream neuroactive derivatives serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598), and the kynurenine-branch intermediate 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632). Biological interpretation implicates perturbation of tryptophan catabolism with secondary effects on neuroactive amine biosynthesis and, marginally, retinoid signalling.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged unambiguously on tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / WP:WP465 / KEGG:map00380 / MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) as the single dominant affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as its top hit (FDR 3.44e-15, 6 of 10 input compounds mapped) and WikiPathways WP:WP465 as rank-1 within its DB (FDR 4.10e-15, 6/62 compounds). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA ranked hsa00380 first by raw p-value (5.41e-09, 6/41 compounds). Mummichog m/z-direct activity returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its top pathway (p=0.004, 13 overlapping m/z features against 14 in the network). No other pathway approached this level of cross-paradigm consensus — the next best Mummichog hit (histidine metabolism) had p=0.037, and MetaboAnalystR's next hit (hsa00830, retinol) had p=0.083. The driver metabolites span both the biosynthetic arm (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine catabolic arm (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), with indoleacetaldehyde and tryptamine representing additional decarboxylation and transamination intermediates. RaMP additionally flagged the more specific Reactome 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.59e-08) and WikiPathways 'Biogenic amine synthesis' (WP:WP550, FDR 3.98e-08) as significant, confirming that the serotonergic/melatonergic branch is the key biological axis altered by the treatment. Molybdenum (C00150, a cofactor for xanthine dehydrogenase) and 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid (C05947) were unresolved by all three tools, suggesting他们是 outliers not embedded in the indexed metabolic networks. 4-Hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) produced a nominal hit in MetaboAnalystR (hsa00830, p=0.083) and in Mummichog (Vitamin A metabolism, p=0.044), but neither reached significance across paradigms, limiting confidence in a separate retinoic-acid story. The tryptophan-metabolism consensus is robust across ORA (two DBs), network m/z (Mummichog), and community-standard KEGG PSEA (MetaboAnalystR). A limitation of this analysis is that two tools (run_sspa_ora and run_fella_rwr) were unavailable at runtime, reducing the total paradigm count below the intended three; however, the three functional tools provided more than sufficient convergence on the winning pathway, and the pathway_members verification tool only supports HUMAN1/RECON2 namespaces, so driver-metabolite membership was cross-validated from the metabolites_hit rosters embedded in the EnrichmentResult objects returned by the ORA and PSEA tools.

RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as its top hit (FDR 3.44e-15, 6 of 10 input compounds mapped) and WikiPathways WP:WP465 as rank-1 within its DB (FDR 4.10e-15, 6/62 compounds). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA ranked hsa00380 first by raw p-value (5.41e-09, 6/41 compounds). Mummichog m/z-direct activity returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its top pathway (p=0.004, 13 overlapping m/z features against 14 in the network). No other pathway approached this level of cross-paradigm consensus — the next best Mummichog hit (histidine metabolism) had p=0.037, and MetaboAnalystR's next hit (hsa00830, retinol) had p=0.083. The driver metabolites span both the biosynthetic arm (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine catabolic arm (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), with indoleacetaldehyde and tryptamine representing additional decarboxylation and transamination intermediates. RaMP additionally flagged the more specific Reactome 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.59e-08) and WikiPathways 'Biogenic amine synthesis' (WP:WP550, FDR 3.98e-08) as significant, confirming that the serotonergic/melatonergic branch is the key biological axis altered by the treatment. Molybdenum (C00150, a cofactor for xanthine dehydrogenase) and 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid (C05947) were unresolved by all three tools, suggesting他们是 outliers not embedded in the indexed metabolic networks. 4-Hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) produced a nominal hit in MetaboAnalystR (hsa00830, p=0.083) and in Mummichog (Vitamin A metabolism, p=0.044), but neither reached significance across paradigms, limiting confidence in a separate retinoic-acid story. The tryptophan-metabolism consensus is robust across ORA (two DBs), network m/z (Mummichog), and community-standard KEGG PSEA (MetaboAnalystR). A limitation of this analysis is that two tools (run_sspa_ora and run_fella_rwr) were unavailable at runtime, reducing the total paradigm count below the intended three; however, the three functional tools provided more than sufficient convergence on the winning pathway, and the pathway_members verification tool only supports HUMAN1/RECON2 namespaces, so driver-metabolite membership was cross-validated from the metabolites_hit rosters embedded in the EnrichmentResult objects returned by the ORA and PSEA tools.
